class.name: NetwDisplayDecl
class.brief_description: One entity's display settings, and what a write to each of them invalidates.
class.description: Every setting is read-only from outside, so [method set_param] is the only door in and the verdict it answers with can never be bypassed by a caller writing a field directly. A role, predicted mode or timeline mode ordinal outside its enum names nothing, so it is refused rather than stored for a pump to meet later. [codeblock] book.write_param(entity, decl, param, value) # -> set_param's verdict, reported through # NetwDisplayBook.mark_dirty as the repair it owes [/codeblock] Params are the ordinals of [code]NetwMultiplayer.DisplayParam[/code], and [member display_role], [member predicted_mode] and [member timeline_mode] are the ordinals of the like-named [NetwDisplayHandle] enums. Those stay the one published spelling, and nothing here publishes a second.

method.name: get_param
method.description: The value of one setting. A [param param] that names no setting is refused and answers [code]null[/code].

method.name: pump_arms_offsets
method.description: Whether a transition from [param previous] to [param next] owes every channel an armed render offset, which is what keeps the displayed value where it is while the new source establishes its first target. A display that was showing nothing has nothing to hold, so [constant PUMP_UNRESOLVED] and [constant PUMP_DISABLED] arm nothing on the way out, and a display going dark has nowhere to hold it, so [constant PUMP_DISABLED] arms nothing on the way in.

method.name: pump_clears_history
method.description: Whether a transition from [param previous] to [param next] invalidates the samples the old pump recorded. Crossing the predicted boundary switches a channel between local sampling and network receive, and the two record in DIFFERENT TICK DOMAINS, so a row from the previous feeder cannot be interpolated against one from the new one. One transition is a warm handoff and keeps its rows: [constant PUMP_CHASE] to [constant PUMP_REMOTE]. A chase ring holds only network rows, already in the remote pump's own tick domain, so a demote resumes from authority instead of holding the last value it wrote.

method.name: pump_for
method.description: Which pump drives a display in [param role], one of [enum Pump]. An authority display and a bracketed prediction share one, because both play back a simulation this peer advances, a tick behind. They differ in what they sample rather than in how it is driven. A chasing prediction is the other pump, and every role that is not one of the three drives nothing, [constant ROLE_AUTO] included: AUTO is a request rather than a role. [member predicted_mode] is read only for [constant ROLE_PREDICTED] and says nothing about any other role.

method.name: pump_is_predicted
method.description: Whether [param pump] drives a display from a simulation this peer advances rather than from a stream it receives.

method.name: set_param
method.description: Writes one setting and answers how much of the display runtime the write invalidated. A [param param] that names no setting, an ordinal outside the enum a setting is drawn from, and a [member visual_root] that is not a path are each refused, change nothing, and answer that nothing was invalidated.

members.member: Seconds a chased visual takes to close the gap to the live body by [code]1/e[/code].
Which display path the entity uses, or [code]0[/code] to resolve it from control and authority.
Whether the buffer may stretch playback to ride out jitter instead of starving.
Smoothing applied to the buffer floor so it settles rather than chases every sample.
How quickly the buffer re-targets when the measured lag moves.
The ceiling on the stretch [member enable_smart_dilation] buys, as a fraction of normal speed.
How far a forecasting timeline may project past the newest sample before it holds.
How a predicted entity turns its body into a pose.
Seconds a predicted visual takes to absorb a correction.
How many starved frames pass before the runtime treats the stream as genuinely stalled.
How much the buffer grows after a starvation, buying margin at the cost of latency.
Where on the timeline a remote entity renders.
How often display tracing samples, or [code]0[/code] to trace nothing.
The child that receives smoothed output, relative to the entity's owner. It is stored as authored, which is what lets a visual be named before the node exists.

constants.constant: The write changed nothing a display runtime has cached.
Which pump the entity runs has to be resolved again.
The runtime has to be rebuilt, which resolves the role on its way through.
Not a pump. It is the state of a runtime whose role has not been resolved yet, which is why it sorts below every real one.
The display runs nothing, because there is nothing here to smooth.
Play back a received stream behind the display clock.
Record the locally advanced simulation each tick and play it back one tick behind, which is what an authority display and a bracketed prediction both do.
Ease the visual toward the live body, which is what a chasing prediction does instead of buffering it.
